ko.B: 젊은 사자들이 그를 보고 으르렁거리며 \q 큰 소리로 울부짖었다. \q 그들이 그의 땅을 폐허로 만들었다. \q 그의 성읍들은 불타 버려 사는 사람이 없다.
ko.R: 원수들이 어린 사자들처럼 그를 향해 으르렁거렸다. \q 그들은 그의 땅을 황무지로 만들었다. \q 그의 성읍들은 불타 버렸고, 아무도 그곳에 살지 않는다.

decisions.choice: young lions: invading armies
decisions.reason: The prophets picture the nations that attack Israel as lions (4:7; 5:6; Isaiah 5:29). In Jeremiah's lifetime the northern kingdom had long since been laid waste by Assyria, and Judah too had lost towns (Isaiah 1:7).

decisions.choice: are burned: the reading tradition's plural
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew has a singular verb and the reading tradition a plural; both mean that the cities are burned. Some take the verb from a related word, "laid waste"; the sense is little changed.

decisions.choice: enemies ... like young lions
decisions.reason: Readable names the enemies the lions stand for (m1) and folds the two lines about their roaring into one.

source.text: גַּם־בְּנֵי־נֹ֖ף וְתַחְפַּנְחֵ֑ס יִרְע֖וּךְ קָדְקֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: Also [the] sons of Memphis and Tahpanhes graze you [on the] crown of [the] head.

en.L: Even the sons of Memphis and Tahpanhes \q graze on the crown of your head.
en.B: Even the people of Memphis and Tahpanhes \q are stripping the crown of your head bare.
en.R: Even the Egyptians from Memphis and Tahpanhes \q are leaving your head stripped bare.

es.L: Aun los hijos de Menfis y de Tafnes \q te pacen la coronilla de la cabeza.
es.B: Aun la gente de Menfis y de Tafnes \q te está dejando pelada la coronilla.
es.R: Aun los egipcios de Menfis y de Tafnes \q te están dejando la cabeza rapada.

fr.L: Même les fils de Memphis et de Tahpanhès \q te tondent le sommet de la tête.
fr.B: Même les gens de Memphis et de Tahpanhès \q te rasent le sommet du crâne.
fr.R: Même les Égyptiens de Memphis et de Tahpanhès \q te laissent la tête rasée.

sw.L: Hata wana wa Memfisi na Tahpanhesi \q wamekunyoa utosi wa kichwa chako.
sw.B: Hata watu wa Memfisi na Tahpanhesi \q wanakinyoa kichwa chako hadi kubaki kipara.
sw.R: Hata Wamisri wa Memfisi na Tahpanhesi \q wanakiacha kichwa chako kikiwa wazi.

vi.L: Ngay cả con cái của Mem-phít và Tác-pha-nết \q cũng gặm trụi đỉnh đầu ngươi.
vi.B: Ngay cả dân Mem-phít và Tác-pha-nết \q cũng đang cạo trọc đỉnh đầu ngươi.
vi.R: Ngay cả người Ai Cập ở Mem-phít và Tác-pha-nết \q cũng đang làm cho đầu ngươi trơ trụi.

ko.L: 놉과 다바네스의 자손들도 \q 네 정수리를 뜯어 먹는다.
ko.B: 멤피스와 다바네스 사람들까지도 \q 네 정수리를 밀어 버리고 있다.
ko.R: 멤피스와 다바네스에서 온 이집트 사람들까지도 \q 네 머리를 밀어 맨머리로 만들고 있다.

decisions.choice: graze: strip bare as cattle strip a field
alternatives: have broken the crown of your head
have shaved the crown of your head
decisions.reason: As the text is written, the verb is "graze" or "feed on": Egypt has cropped the crown of Israel's head bare, a picture of shame and loss. The same consonants can also be read as "break" or "crush" ("have broken the crown of your head"), and some have suggested "shave", a sign of disgrace. The sense is uncertain.

decisions.choice: Memphis and Tahpanhes: cities of Egypt
decisions.reason: Memphis (in Hebrew *Noph*) was the old capital of Lower Egypt, and Tahpanhes a border fortress in the eastern delta, where Jeremiah was later taken (43:7-9). Judah looked to Egypt for help, but Egypt too brought it harm. In Jeremiah's youth Pharaoh Neco killed King Josiah and put Judah under tribute (2 Kings 23:29-35). The written text and the reading tradition spell Tahpanhes slightly differently.

decisions.choice: sons (Literal); people (Balanced); the Egyptians (Readable); graze / stripping bare / leaving stripped bare
decisions.reason: "Sons of" a city means its people. Balanced and Readable give the sense of the grazing picture (m1); Readable names the people as Egyptians.

decisions.choice: "Menfis", "Tafnes"; "te pacen" (L); "te está dejando pelada" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Egyptian cities in their usual Spanish forms ("Tafnes", as the terms note gives it). Literal keeps the picture of cattle grazing; Balanced and Readable say it means stripping bare, as the English does. From here Israel is addressed as a woman, "tú".

decisions.choice: Memfisi, Tahpanhesi
decisions.reason: The English names the city Memphis at every level; Swahili gives its usual name "Memfisi" rather than a transliteration of the Hebrew Noph, and Tahpanhes in the form the terms note sets.

decisions.choice: wamekunyoa (Literal); wanakinyoa ... kipara (Balanced); wanakiacha ... wazi (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Graze" is pictured as shaving the head bare, a mark of shame in Swahili too; the grazing image does not carry over on the head.

decisions.choice: "Memphis", "Tahpanhès"; "te tondent" (L); "te rasent" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Memphis is the usual French name of the city the Hebrew calls Noph; "tondre" keeps the picture of stripping bare (m1) in a verb French uses of a head, where "brouter" would not be understood.

decisions.choice: "Mem-phít" (Memphis) and "Tác-pha-nết" (Tahpanhes)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "Noph" is Memphis, and the English names it so; "Mem-phít" is the form used for it throughout Isaiah and Jeremiah (Isaiah 19:13; Jeremiah 44:1; 46:14, 19). "Tác-pha-nết" is the terms note's form. Readable says "người Ai Cập", as the English does.

decisions.choice: 놉 (Literal); 멤피스 (Balanced, Readable); 다바네스
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew name of the Egyptian city in its Protestant form; Balanced and Readable give the name a modern reader knows, as the English does. Tahpanhes is 다바네스 at every level, as the terms note.

source.text: הֲלוֹא־זֹ֖את תַּעֲשֶׂה־לָּ֑ךְ עָזְבֵךְ֙ אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהַ֔יִךְ בְּעֵ֖ת מוֹלִיכֵ֥ךְ בַּדָּֽרֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: [Is it] not this [that] you do to yourself, [by] your forsaking Yahweh your God at [the] time [he was] leading you in the way?

en.L: Have you not done this to yourself \q by forsaking {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God \q at the time when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was leading you in the way?
en.B: Is this not what you have done to yourself \q in forsaking {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God \q while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was leading you on the way?
en.R: You have brought this trouble on yourself! \q You turned away from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God \q while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was leading you on the right road.

es.L: ¿No te has hecho esto a ti misma \q al abandonar {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} tu Dios \q en el tiempo en que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} te guiaba por el camino?
es.B: ¿No es esto lo que te has hecho a ti misma \q al abandonar {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} tu Dios \q cuando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} te guiaba por el camino?
es.R: ¡Tú misma te has buscado este problema! \q Le diste la espalda {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} tu Dios \q cuando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} te guiaba por el buen camino.

fr.L: N’est-ce pas cela que tu t’es fait à toi-même, \q en abandonnant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu \q au temps où {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} te conduisait dans le chemin ?
fr.B: N’est-ce pas toi qui t’es attiré cela, \q en abandonnant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu \q alors qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} te guidait sur la route ?
fr.R: C’est toi-même qui as causé ce malheur ! \q Tu t’es détournée {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ton Dieu \q alors qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} te conduisait sur le bon chemin.

sw.L: Je, hukujitendea haya wewe mwenyewe \q kwa kumwacha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako \q wakati alipokuwa akikuongoza njiani?
sw.B: Je, hili si jambo ulilojitendea wewe mwenyewe \q kwa kumwacha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako \q wakati {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alipokuwa akikuongoza njiani?
sw.R: Wewe mwenyewe umejiletea taabu hii! \q Ulimwacha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako \q wakati {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alipokuwa akikuongoza katika njia iliyo sawa.

vi.L: Chẳng phải ngươi tự gây điều này cho mình \q khi ngươi lìa bỏ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi \q vào lúc {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang dẫn ngươi đi trên đường sao?
vi.B: Chẳng phải chính ngươi đã tự chuốc lấy điều này \q khi lìa bỏ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi \q trong lúc {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang dẫn ngươi đi trên đường sao?
vi.R: Chính ngươi đã tự chuốc lấy tai họa này! \q Ngươi đã quay lưng với {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi \q trong khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang dẫn ngươi đi đúng đường.

ko.L: 이것은 네가 너 자신에게 한 일이 아니냐? \q 네 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 버림으로써, \q 그가 너를 길로 인도하던 그때에.
ko.B: 이것은 네가 스스로 불러들인 일이 아니냐? \q 너는 네 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 버렸다. \q 그가 너를 길로 인도하고 있을 때에 말이다.
ko.R: 너는 이 어려움을 스스로 불러들였다! \q 너는 네 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 떠났다. \q 그가 너를 바른 길로 이끌고 있었는데도 그렇게 했다.

decisions.choice: Have you not done this to yourself?: a question that expects the answer yes
decisions.reason: The question answers verse 14. Israel's ruin is not bad luck or God's failure; it is the result of leaving the God who was guiding it (verse 19).

decisions.choice: leading you in the way: God guiding his people as on a journey
decisions.reason: The words recall God leading Israel through the wilderness (verse 6; Deuteronomy 1:31-33; 8:2) and point to his guidance in the way of life he taught. They left him in the middle of the journey.

decisions.choice: You have brought this trouble on yourself! ... the right road
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into the statement it implies (m1) and adds "right" to show what "the way" means here.

decisions.choice: ngươi (every level), to Jerusalem in this rebuke
decisions.reason: God's address to Jerusalem, Israel or Judah as one person follows one rule in Isaiah and Jeremiah: "ngươi" at every level in rebukes and sentences of judgment (Jeremiah 2:2-3:5; 4:7-31; 5:7; 6:8, 23; 7:29; 11:15-16; 13:20-27; 15:5-14; 17:3-4), and "ngươi" (Literal) / "con" (Balanced, Readable) in appeals and promises (3:12-19; 4:1-2; 30-31). Chapter 2 is a lawsuit against Jerusalem, so even the opening memory of her early love (2:2) keeps "ngươi".

decisions.choice: 그가 너를 인도하던 (no honorific -시-)
decisions.reason: The oracle is God's own speech (verse 19 ends "declares the Lord GOD"), so where God speaks of himself in the third person Korean keeps his own speech level and does not give himself the honorific, as with 주가 말한다.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה מַה־לָּךְ֙ לְדֶ֣רֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם לִשְׁתּ֖וֹת מֵ֣י שִׁח֑וֹר וּמַה־לָּךְ֙ לְדֶ֣רֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר לִשְׁתּ֖וֹת מֵ֥י נָהָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And now what [is it] to you to [the] way of Egypt, to drink [the] waters of Shihor? And what [is it] to you to [the] way of Assyria, to drink [the] waters of [the] River?

en.L: And now, what [is it] to you [to go] on the road to Egypt, \q to drink the waters of Shihor? \q And what [is it] to you [to go] on the road to Assyria, \q to drink the waters of the River?
en.B: So now, what do you gain by taking the road to Egypt \q to drink the waters of the Shihor? \q What do you gain by taking the road to Assyria \q to drink the waters of the Euphrates?
en.R: So why go down the road to Egypt \q to drink water from the Nile? \q Why go off on the road to Assyria \q to drink water from the Euphrates River?

es.L: Y ahora, ¿qué [tienes] tú con el camino a Egipto, \q para beber las aguas del Sihor? \q ¿Y qué [tienes] tú con el camino a Asiria, \q para beber las aguas del Río?
es.B: Y ahora, ¿qué ganas con tomar el camino a Egipto \q para beber las aguas del Sihor? \q ¿Qué ganas con tomar el camino a Asiria \q para beber las aguas del Éufrates?
es.R: Entonces, ¿para qué bajas por el camino a Egipto \q a beber agua del Nilo? \q ¿Para qué te vas por el camino a Asiria \q a beber agua del río Éufrates?

fr.L: Et maintenant, qu’as-tu [à faire] sur le chemin de l’Égypte, \q pour boire les eaux du Shihor ? \q Et qu’as-tu [à faire] sur le chemin de l’Assyrie, \q pour boire les eaux du Fleuve ?
fr.B: Et maintenant, que gagnes-tu à prendre le chemin de l’Égypte \q pour boire les eaux du Shihor ? \q Que gagnes-tu à prendre le chemin de l’Assyrie \q pour boire les eaux de l’Euphrate ?
fr.R: Alors pourquoi prendre la route de l’Égypte \q pour boire l’eau du Nil ? \q Pourquoi partir sur la route de l’Assyrie \q pour boire l’eau du fleuve Euphrate ?

sw.L: Na sasa, una nini wewe na njia ya Misri, \q kunywa maji ya Shihori? \q Na una nini wewe na njia ya Ashuru, \q kunywa maji ya Mto?
sw.B: Basi sasa, utapata faida gani kwa kuishika njia ya Misri \q ili kunywa maji ya Shihori? \q Utapata faida gani kwa kuishika njia ya Ashuru \q ili kunywa maji ya mto Frati?
sw.R: Basi kwa nini kwenda katika njia ya Misri \q kunywa maji ya mto Naili? \q Kwa nini kwenda katika njia ya Ashuru \q kunywa maji ya mto Frati?

vi.L: Và bây giờ, ngươi [đi] trên đường đến Ai Cập để làm gì, \q để uống nước Si-ho sao? \q Ngươi [đi] trên đường đến A-si-ri để làm gì, \q để uống nước của Sông sao?
vi.B: Vậy bây giờ, ngươi được gì khi đi đường xuống Ai Cập \q để uống nước sông Si-ho? \q Ngươi được gì khi đi đường sang A-si-ri \q để uống nước sông Ơ-phơ-rát?
vi.R: Vậy tại sao ngươi lại đi xuống đường Ai Cập \q để uống nước sông Nin? \q Tại sao ngươi lại đi lên đường A-si-ri \q để uống nước sông Ơ-phơ-rát?

ko.L: 그런데 이제 네가 이집트로 가는 길에 [나선 것이] 무슨 일이냐? \q 시홀의 물을 마시려는 것이냐? \q 또 네가 앗시리아로 가는 길에 [나선 것이] 무슨 일이냐? \q 그 강의 물을 마시려는 것이냐?
ko.B: 그런데 이제 네가 이집트로 가는 길에 나서서 \q 시홀 강물을 마신들 무슨 소용이 있느냐? \q 앗시리아로 가는 길에 나서서 \q 유프라테스 강물을 마신들 무슨 소용이 있느냐?
ko.R: 그런데 왜 이집트로 가는 길로 내려가서 \q 나일 강물을 마시려 하느냐? \q 왜 앗시리아로 가는 길로 떠나서 \q 유프라테스 강물을 마시려 하느냐?

decisions.choice: Shihor and the River: the Nile and the Euphrates
decisions.reason: Shihor was a branch or channel of the Nile on Egypt's eastern edge (Joshua 13:3; Isaiah 23:3), and "the River" is the Euphrates, the river of Mesopotamia (Genesis 31:21). Each river stands for the great power that lived by it.

decisions.choice: to drink the waters: to seek help from Egypt and Assyria
decisions.reason: Judah's kings looked to Egypt and to Assyria by turns for protection and paid them for it (2 Kings 16:7-8; 17:4; Hosea 7:11). The picture of drinking points back to verse 13: they left the spring of living water to drink from foreign rivers.

decisions.choice: what is it to you?: what business do you have, what good will it do
decisions.reason: The question asks what reason they have to go, and what they hope to gain. It expects the answer: none.

decisions.choice: Shihor (Literal), the Shihor (Balanced), the Nile (Readable); the River (Literal), the Euphrates (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for "the River", as in Isaiah. Readable names the Shihor by its river, the Nile (m1).

decisions.choice: "el Sihor" (L, B), "el Nilo" (R); "el Río" (L), "el Éufrates" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the English levels: Literal keeps the Hebrew names, Balanced names the Euphrates, Readable names both rivers.

decisions.choice: Shihori (Literal, Balanced), mto Naili (Readable); Mto (Literal), mto Frati (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The rivers named as the English levels name them; "Shihori" as Joshua 13:3 and "mto Frati" as 1 Kings 14:15.

decisions.choice: "le Shihor" (L, B), "le Nil" (R); "le Fleuve" (L), "l’Euphrate" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for "the River" in the prophets: Literal keeps the title, capitalised as a name, and Balanced and Readable name it, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "Si-ho" (Literal, Balanced), "sông Nin" (Readable); "Sông" (Literal), "sông Ơ-phơ-rát" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As the English levels: Literal keeps the Hebrew names, Balanced names the Euphrates, Readable names both rivers. "Si-ho" is the published form (Joshua 13:3).

decisions.choice: 시홀 ... 그 강 (Literal); 시홀 강 ... 유프라테스 강 (Balanced); 나일 강 ... 유프라테스 강 (Readable)
alternatives: | As the English: Literal keeps the Hebrew names, Balanced names the River, and Readable names both rivers as a reader knows them.

source.text: תְּיַסְּרֵ֣ךְ רָעָתֵ֗ךְ וּמְשֻֽׁבוֹתַ֨יִךְ֙ תּוֹכִחֻ֔ךְ וּדְעִ֤י וּרְאִי֙ כִּי־רַ֣ע וָמָ֔ר עָזְבֵ֖ךְ אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֑יִךְ וְלֹ֤א פַחְדָּתִי֙ אֵלַ֔יִךְ נְאֻם־אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: Will discipline you your evil, and your turnings away will rebuke you; and know and see that evil and bitter [is] your forsaking Yahweh your God, and not [is] dread of me toward you, declares [the] Lord Yahweh of hosts.

en.L: Your evil will discipline you, and your turnings away will rebuke you. \q Know and see that it is evil and bitter \q for you to forsake {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, \q and that the dread of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is not in you, \q declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of hosts.
en.B: Your own wickedness will punish you, and your turning away will convict you. \q Know, then, and see what an evil and bitter thing it is \q for you to forsake {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, \q with no dread of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in you, \q declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of Armies.
en.R: Your own evil will punish you. Your turning away will prove you wrong. \q Understand this and see it clearly: \q it is evil and bitter to leave {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God \q and to have no fear of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

es.L: Tu maldad te castigará, y tus apostasías te reprenderán. \q Sabe, pues, y mira que es malo y amargo \q que abandones {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} tu Dios, \q y que no haya temor de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} en ti, \q declara el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos.
es.B: Tu propia maldad te castigará, y tu apostasía te acusará. \q Reconoce, pues, y mira qué cosa tan mala y amarga es \q abandonar {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} tu Dios \q y no tener temor de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, \q afirma el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos.
es.R: Tu propio mal te castigará. Tu infidelidad te dejará en evidencia. \q Entiende esto y míralo claramente: \q es malo y amargo dejar {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} tu Dios \q y no tener temor de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, \q dice el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos.

fr.L: Ta méchanceté te corrigera, et tes infidélités te réprimanderont. \q Sache et vois qu’il est mauvais et amer \q d’abandonner {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu, \q et que la crainte de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} n’est pas en toi, \q déclare le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} des armées.
fr.B: Ta propre méchanceté te punira, et tes infidélités te condamneront. \q Reconnais donc et vois combien il est mauvais et amer \q d’abandonner {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu, \q sans avoir aucune crainte de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, \q déclare le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} des armées.
fr.R: Ton propre mal te punira. Ton infidélité montrera que tu as tort. \q Comprends-le et vois-le clairement : \q c’est mauvais et amer d’abandonner {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu \q et de ne pas avoir de respect pour {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, \q dit le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} des armées.

sw.L: Uovu wako utakuadhibu, na maasi yako yatakukemea. \q Basi ujue na kuona ya kuwa ni uovu na uchungu \q kumwacha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako, \q na kwamba kunicha {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} hakumo ndani yako, \q asema Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.
sw.B: Uovu wako mwenyewe utakuadhibu, na kuniacha kwako kutakuhukumu. \q Basi jua na uone jinsi lilivyo jambo baya na chungu \q wewe kumwacha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako, \q bila kuwa na hofu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} ndani yako, \q asema Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.
sw.R: Uovu wako mwenyewe utakuadhibu. Kuniacha kwako kutaonyesha kwamba umekosea. \q Elewa jambo hili na ulione wazi: \q ni jambo baya na chungu kumwacha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako \q na kutoniogopa {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, \q anasema Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.

vi.L: Điều ác của ngươi sẽ sửa phạt ngươi, và sự bội nghịch của ngươi sẽ quở trách ngươi. \q Hãy biết và thấy rằng thật là xấu xa và cay đắng \q khi ngươi lìa bỏ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi, \q và sự kính sợ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không ở trong ngươi, \q Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán vậy.
vi.B: Chính sự gian ác của ngươi sẽ trừng phạt ngươi, sự bội nghịch của ngươi sẽ buộc tội ngươi. \q Vậy hãy biết và thấy rằng thật là xấu xa và cay đắng \q khi ngươi lìa bỏ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi, \q chẳng còn chút kính sợ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, \q Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán vậy.
vi.R: Chính điều ác của ngươi sẽ trừng phạt ngươi. Sự quay lưng của ngươi sẽ cho thấy ngươi sai. \q Hãy hiểu điều này và thấy cho rõ: \q lìa bỏ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của ngươi \q và không kính sợ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là điều xấu xa và cay đắng, \q Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán.

ko.L: 네 악이 너를 징계하고, 네 돌아섬들이 너를 책망할 것이다. \q 그러니 알고 보아라. 악하고 쓴 일이다. \q 네가 네 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 버린 것과 \q 나에 대한 두려움이 네게 없는 것은. \q 만군의 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}의 선언이다.
ko.B: 네 악이 너를 벌하고, 네가 나에게서 돌아선 일이 너를 꾸짖을 것이다. \q 그러니 깨달아 알아라. \q 네 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 버리고 \q 나를 두려워하지 않는 것이 얼마나 악하고 쓰라린 일인지를. \q 만군의 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.R: 네 악이 너를 벌할 것이다. 나에게서 돌아선 일이 네 잘못을 드러낼 것이다. \q 이것을 깨닫고 똑똑히 보아라. \q 네 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 떠나 \q 나를 두려워하지 않는 것은 악하고 쓰라린 일이다. \q 하늘의 군대를 거느린 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}가 말한다.

decisions.choice: turnings away: unfaithfulness, a people turning back from God
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "turn" and means turning away, backsliding. It is one of Jeremiah's key words (3:6-22; 5:6; 8:5), set against the turning back to God he calls for.

decisions.choice: your evil will discipline you: sin brings its own punishment
decisions.reason: The two verbs belong to a parent or teacher correcting a child (verse 30). The disasters that come on Judah are the results of its own choices, and they are meant to teach it.

decisions.choice: the dread of me: reverent fear of God
decisions.reason: The rare word means trembling awe. To fear God is to take him seriously as the holy one and to obey him (5:22-24).

decisions.choice: the Lord GOD of hosts (Literal); the Lord GOD of Armies (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for this title, as in Isaiah. The divine name follows "Lord" here, so it is printed GOD.

decisions.choice: "el Señor DIOS de los ejércitos" (L); "el Señor DIOS de los Ejércitos" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Adonai YHWH of hosts as the terms note sets it for Spanish: lowercase "ejércitos" at Literal, capitalized as a title at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: Bwana MUNGU wa majeshi
decisions.reason: "BWANA wa majeshi" stands at every level in Swahili (Samuel, Psalms), where the English Balanced and Readable say "of Armies"; "the Lord GOD" is "Bwana MUNGU" as the terms note.

decisions.choice: "le Seigneur DIEU des armées" at every level, as "le SEIGNEUR des armées", for the whole book
decisions.reason: French keeps "des armées" at every level, as Samuel, the Psalms and 2 Kings 19:31 do, where the English Balanced and Readable say "of Armies".

decisions.choice: "Chúa là CHÚA Vạn Quân" at every level
alternatives: "Chúa là CHÚA của các đạo quân"
decisions.reason: Adonai YHWH is "Chúa là CHÚA" (Samuel, Psalms), and "of hosts" is "Vạn Quân" at every level (terms note), so the English Literal/Balanced difference does not arise.

decisions.choice: 만군의 주 하나님 (Literal, Balanced); 하늘의 군대를 거느린 주 하나님 (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Lord GOD of hosts follows the terms note (Psalm 69:7 B), with the setting on 하나님; in God's own mouth the Readable form is 거느린, without -시-.

source.text: כִּ֣י מֵעוֹלָ֞ם שָׁבַ֣רְתִּי עֻלֵּ֗ךְ נִתַּ֨קְתִּי֙ מוֹסְרֹתַ֔יִךְ וַתֹּאמְרִ֖י לֹ֣א אֶעֱב֑וֹר כִּ֣י עַֽל־כָּל־גִּבְעָ֞ה גְּבֹהָ֗ה וְתַ֨חַת֙ כָּל־עֵ֣ץ רַעֲנָ֔ן אַ֖תְּ צֹעָ֥ה זֹנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: For from long ago I broke your yoke, I tore off your bonds, and you said, Not I will transgress; for on every hill high and under every tree green you [were] lying down, a prostitute.

en.L: For long ago I broke your yoke [and] tore off your bonds, \q and you said, "I will not transgress." \q Yet on every high hill and under every green tree \q you lay down, a prostitute.
en.B: Long ago I broke your yoke and tore off your chains, \q and you said, "I will not transgress." \q Yet on every high hill and under every leafy tree \q you sprawled like a prostitute.
en.R: Long ago I broke the yoke that held you and tore off your chains. \q You said, "I will never disobey." \q But on every high hill and beneath every green tree \q you lay down like a prostitute to worship other gods.

es.L: Porque desde antiguo quebré tu yugo [y] rompí tus ataduras, \q y dijiste: «No transgrediré». \q Sin embargo, sobre toda colina alta y debajo de todo árbol frondoso \q te acostabas, prostituta.
es.B: Hace mucho tiempo quebré tu yugo y rompí tus cadenas, \q y dijiste: «No pecaré». \q Pero sobre toda colina alta y bajo todo árbol frondoso \q te tendías como una prostituta.
es.R: Hace mucho tiempo rompí el yugo que te sujetaba y quité tus cadenas. \q Dijiste: «Nunca desobedeceré». \q Pero sobre cada colina alta y debajo de cada árbol verde \q te acostabas como una prostituta para adorar a otros dioses.

fr.L: Car depuis longtemps j’ai brisé ton joug, j’ai arraché tes liens, \q et tu as dit : « Je ne transgresserai pas. » \q Pourtant, sur toute colline élevée et sous tout arbre vert, \q tu t’es couchée, prostituée.
fr.B: Depuis longtemps j’ai brisé ton joug et arraché tes chaînes, \q et tu as dit : « Je ne transgresserai pas. » \q Pourtant, sur toute colline élevée et sous tout arbre feuillu, \q tu t’es vautrée comme une prostituée.
fr.R: Il y a longtemps, j’ai brisé le joug qui t’écrasait et j’ai arraché tes chaînes. \q Tu as dit : « Je ne désobéirai jamais. » \q Mais sur toutes les hautes collines et sous tous les arbres verts, \q tu t’es couchée comme une prostituée pour adorer d’autres dieux.

sw.L: Kwa maana tangu zamani nilivunja nira yako, nikakata vifungo vyako, \q nawe ukasema, "Sitakosa." \q Lakini juu ya kila kilima kirefu na chini ya kila mti mbichi \q ulijilaza, kahaba.
sw.B: Zamani nilivunja nira yako na kukata minyororo yako, \q nawe ukasema, "Sitakosa." \q Lakini juu ya kila kilima kirefu na chini ya kila mti wenye majani mengi \q ulijilaza kama kahaba.
sw.R: Zamani nilivunja nira iliyokubana na kukata minyororo yako. \q Ulisema, "Sitakuasi kamwe." \q Lakini juu ya kila kilima kirefu na chini ya kila mti wenye majani mabichi \q ulijilaza kama kahaba ili kuabudu miungu mingine.

vi.L: Vì từ xưa {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã bẻ ách ngươi, đã bứt dây trói ngươi, \q và ngươi đã nói: "Tôi sẽ không vi phạm." \q Thế mà trên mọi đồi cao và dưới mọi cây xanh, \q ngươi đã nằm xuống, làm gái điếm.
vi.B: Từ lâu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã bẻ gãy ách của ngươi, bứt đứt xiềng xích của ngươi, \q và ngươi đã nói: "Tôi sẽ không vi phạm." \q Thế mà trên mọi đồi cao và dưới mọi cây rậm lá, \q ngươi đã nằm dài như một gái điếm.
vi.R: Từ lâu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã bẻ gãy cái ách đè trên ngươi và bứt đứt xiềng xích ngươi. \q Ngươi đã nói: "Tôi sẽ không bao giờ bất tuân." \q Nhưng trên mọi đồi cao và dưới mọi cây xanh, \q ngươi đã nằm xuống như gái điếm để thờ các thần khác.

ko.L: 내가 오래전에 네 멍에를 꺾고 네 결박을 끊었다. \q 그러자 너는 "나는 범하지 않겠다" 하고 말했다. \q 그러나 너는 높은 언덕마다, 푸른 나무 아래마다 \q 창녀가 되어 누웠다.
ko.B: 오래전에 내가 네 멍에를 꺾고 네 사슬을 끊어 주었다. \q 그때 너는 "나는 죄를 짓지 않겠다" 하고 말했다. \q 그런데도 너는 높은 언덕마다, 잎이 무성한 나무 아래마다 \q 창녀처럼 몸을 눕혔다.
ko.R: 오래전에 나는 너를 묶고 있던 멍에를 꺾고 네 사슬을 끊어 주었다. \q 너는 "나는 결코 거역하지 않겠다" 하고 말했다. \q 그러나 너는 높은 언덕마다, 푸른 나무 아래마다 \q 창녀처럼 누워 다른 신들을 섬겼다.

decisions.choice: I will not transgress: the reading of the text as pointed
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew and the reading tradition differ by one letter here, and the two forms give "I will not transgress" and "I will not serve". The text followed here reads "transgress": set free from Egypt, Israel promised not to break the covenant (Exodus 24:3, 7), and then broke it on every hill. The Greek translation has "I will not serve", a refusal to serve God.

decisions.choice: I broke ... I tore off: God freed Israel
alternatives: you broke your yoke and tore off your bonds
decisions.reason: The verbs are first person as the text is pointed: God broke the yoke of Egypt (Leviticus 26:13). The same spelling can be an older form of "you" said to a woman, and the Greek reads it so: "you broke your yoke ... and said, I will not serve", that is, Israel threw off God's yoke (5:5).

decisions.choice: every high hill and every green tree: the places of Canaanite worship
decisions.reason: Shrines to Baal and Asherah stood on hilltops and under leafy trees (Deuteronomy 12:2; 1 Kings 14:23; 2 Kings 17:10). Worship there could include ritual sex, and the prophets call all such worship prostitution: unfaithfulness to the God who is Israel's husband (3:1-2, 6; Hosea 4:13).

decisions.choice: yoke ... bonds: slavery
decisions.reason: A yoke and its straps held an animal to its work. Breaking them means release from bondage, as from Egypt (Leviticus 26:13; Ezekiel 34:27).

decisions.choice: never disobey ... to worship other gods
decisions.reason: Readable says "disobey" for "transgress" and adds what the lying down was for (m3), so the picture is not taken as plain prostitution only.

decisions.choice: "ách" (yoke)
decisions.reason: "Cái ách" is the terms note's word for the yoke (1 Kings 12:4), kept for Jeremiah 27-28 as well.

decisions.choice: 멍에
decisions.reason: The yoke is 멍에 at every level, as the terms note and 1 Kings 12, so that this verse links with the yoke of chapters 27-28.

source.text: וְאָֽנֹכִי֙ נְטַעְתִּ֣יךְ שֹׂרֵ֔ק כֻּלֹּ֖ה זֶ֣רַע אֱמֶ֑ת וְאֵיךְ֙ נֶהְפַּ֣כְתְּ לִ֔י סוּרֵ֖י הַגֶּ֥פֶן נָכְרִיָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And I planted you [as] a choice vine, all of it seed of truth; and how have you turned to me [into] degenerate [shoots] of the vine foreign?

en.L: Yet I planted you a choice vine, \q all of it true seed. \q How then have you turned, before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q into the degenerate shoots of a foreign vine?
en.B: I planted you as a choice vine, \q from seed that was wholly true. \q How then have you turned, before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q into the wild shoots of a strange vine?
en.R: I planted you like the best kind of grapevine, \q grown from good, pure seed. \q So how could you turn into \q a wild vine that is no good to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?

es.L: Yo te planté como vid escogida, \q toda ella simiente verdadera. \q ¿Cómo, pues, te has vuelto delante de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} \q sarmientos degenerados de vid extraña?
es.B: Yo te planté como una vid escogida, \q de una semilla del todo buena. \q ¿Cómo, pues, te has convertido delante de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} \q en los brotes silvestres de una vid extraña?
es.R: Te planté como la mejor clase de vid, \q nacida de semilla buena y pura. \q Entonces, ¿cómo pudiste convertirte \q en una vid silvestre que no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} sirve para nada?

fr.L: Pourtant je t’avais plantée [comme] une vigne de choix, \q tout entière d’une semence vraie. \q Comment t’es-tu changée, devant {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, \q en sarments dégénérés d’une vigne étrangère ?
fr.B: Je t’avais plantée comme une vigne de choix, \q d’une semence entièrement sûre. \q Comment t’es-tu changée, devant {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, \q en rejets sauvages d’une vigne étrangère ?
fr.R: Je t’avais plantée comme la meilleure sorte de vigne, \q poussée d’une bonne semence, bien pure. \q Alors comment as-tu pu devenir \q une vigne sauvage qui ne {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} sert à rien ?

sw.L: Nami nilikupanda mzabibu mteule, \q wote mbegu ya kweli. \q Basi umegeukaje mbele {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} \q kuwa machipukizi yaliyoharibika ya mzabibu mgeni?
sw.B: Nilikupanda kama mzabibu bora, \q kutoka mbegu iliyo safi kabisa. \q Basi umegeukaje mbele {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} \q kuwa machipukizi pori ya mzabibu mgeni?
sw.R: Nilikupanda kama mzabibu wa aina iliyo bora, \q uliootesha kutoka mbegu nzuri na safi. \q Basi umewezaje kugeuka \q kuwa mzabibu pori usio na faida yoyote kwangu?

vi.L: Ta đã trồng ngươi như một gốc nho quý, \q hoàn toàn là giống thật. \q Sao ngươi lại biến đổi trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} \q thành những nhánh thoái hóa của cây nho lạ?
vi.B: Ta đã trồng ngươi như một cây nho quý, \q từ giống hoàn toàn thuần chủng. \q Vậy sao trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ngươi lại biến thành \q những nhánh dại của một cây nho lạ?
vi.R: Ta đã trồng ngươi như giống nho tốt nhất, \q mọc lên từ hạt giống tốt và thuần. \q Vậy sao ngươi lại biến thành \q một cây nho dại chẳng dùng được gì cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}?

ko.L: 나는 너를 귀한 포도나무로, \q 모두 참된 씨로 심었다. \q 그런데 어떻게 네가 내 앞에서 \q 낯선 포도나무의 썩은 가지로 변했느냐?
ko.B: 나는 너를 좋은 품종의 포도나무로, \q 온전히 참된 씨에서 난 것으로 심었다. \q 그런데 어찌하여 너는 내 앞에서 \q 낯선 포도나무의 들가지로 변해 버렸느냐?
ko.R: 나는 너를 가장 좋은 포도나무처럼, \q 좋고 깨끗한 씨에서 자라게 심었다. \q 그런데 어떻게 네가 \q 나에게 아무 쓸모없는 들포도나무가 되어 버렸느냐?

decisions.choice: a choice vine: a vine of the finest red grapes
decisions.reason: The word names a prized kind of vine (Isaiah 5:2; Genesis 49:11). A farmer planted it to get the best wine.

decisions.choice: I planted you a vine: Israel as God's vineyard
decisions.reason: Israel is often pictured as a vine God planted (Psalm 80:9-17; Hosea 10:1). Isaiah's song of the vineyard tells the same story: God planted the best vine and it gave wild grapes (Isaiah 5:1-7).

decisions.choice: true seed: reliable stock, sure to grow true to kind
decisions.reason: The word *'emet* means what is firm and dependable. The seed was pure, so the change in the vine was not the planter's fault.

decisions.choice: degenerate shoots of a foreign vine: a wild, worthless growth
decisions.reason: The first word means turned aside, gone bad, and "foreign" means strange, unlike what was planted. The good vine has become something wild that gives no good fruit.

decisions.choice: a wild vine that is no good to me
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of "degenerate" and "foreign" (m4) in plain words, and folds "to me" into "no good to me".

source.text: כִּ֤י אִם־תְּכַבְּסִי֙ בַּנֶּ֔תֶר וְתַרְבִּי־לָ֖ךְ בֹּרִ֑ית נִכְתָּ֤ם עֲוֺנֵךְ֙ לְפָנַ֔י נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: For even if you wash with lye and make much for yourself soap, stained [is] your iniquity before me, declares [the] Lord Yahweh.

en.L: For even if you wash with lye \q and use much soap for yourself, \q your iniquity is stained before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Even if you scrub yourself with washing soda \q and use soap in plenty, \q your guilt remains a stain before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: You may scrub yourself with strong soap \q and use as much of it as you like, \q but I can still see the stain of your sin, \q says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Aunque te laves con lejía \q y uses para ti mucho jabón, \q manchada [está] tu iniquidad delante de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, \q declara el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}.
es.B: Aunque te frotes con sosa \q y uses jabón en abundancia, \q tu culpa sigue siendo una mancha delante de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, \q afirma el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}.
es.R: Puedes restregarte con jabón fuerte \q y usar todo el que quieras, \q pero yo sigo viendo la mancha de tu pecado, \q dice el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Car même si tu te lavais avec du nitre \q et que tu employais beaucoup de savon, \q ta faute resterait une tache devant {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, \q déclare le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Même si tu te frottais avec de la soude \q et que tu prenais du savon en abondance, \q ta faute resterait une tache devant {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, \q déclare le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Tu peux te frotter avec un savon très fort \q et en mettre autant que tu veux, \q je vois encore la tache de ton péché, \q dit le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Kwa maana hata ukijiosha kwa magadi \q na kujitumia sabuni nyingi, \q uovu wako una doa mbele {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, \q asema Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Hata ukijisugua kwa magadi \q na kutumia sabuni kwa wingi, \q hatia yako inabaki kuwa doa mbele {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, \q asema Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Unaweza kujisugua kwa sabuni kali \q na kuitumia kwa wingi kama upendavyo, \q lakini bado ninaliona doa la dhambi yako, \q anasema Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}}.

vi.L: Dù ngươi rửa bằng nước tro \q và dùng nhiều xà phòng cho mình, \q tội ác ngươi vẫn còn vết dơ trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, \q Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.B: Dù ngươi có kỳ cọ bằng xút \q và dùng thật nhiều xà phòng, \q tội lỗi ngươi vẫn còn là vết bẩn trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, \q Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.R: Dù ngươi có chà rửa bằng xà phòng thật mạnh \q và dùng bao nhiêu tùy thích, \q Ta vẫn thấy vết nhơ tội lỗi của ngươi, \q Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán.

ko.L: 네가 잿물로 씻고 \q 비누를 많이 쓸지라도, \q 네 죄악은 내 앞에 얼룩져 있다. \q 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}의 선언이다.
ko.B: 네가 세탁 소다로 문질러 씻고 \q 비누를 아무리 많이 쓴다 해도, \q 네 죄는 내 앞에 얼룩으로 남아 있다. \q 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.R: 네가 독한 비누로 몸을 문지르고 \q 그것을 마음껏 쓴다 해도, \q 나는 여전히 네 죄의 얼룩을 본다. \q 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}가 말한다.

decisions.choice: lye and soap: strong cleaning agents
decisions.reason: The first word is natron, a natural mineral soda used for washing. The second is a cleanser made from the ashes of plants (Malachi 3:2). They were the strongest cleaners people had; even they could not remove this stain.

decisions.choice: stained: marked with a stain that will not come out
decisions.reason: The verb, found only here, means to be stained or marked. Sin is pictured as a dirt that sticks; Judah cannot wash it away by its own efforts, though God can (33:8; Psalm 51:4, 9).

decisions.choice: lye / washing soda / strong soap; iniquity / guilt / sin
decisions.reason: The levels name the cleaner in more familiar words. *'Awon* follows the settled wording: iniquity, guilt, sin.

decisions.choice: "nitre" (L); "soude" (B); "un savon très fort" (R); "faute" (L, B), "péché" (R) for *ʿawon*
decisions.reason: The levels name the cleaner in more familiar words, as the English does; *ʿawon* is "la faute" in the French of the Pentateuch.

source.text: אֵ֣יךְ תֹּאמְרִ֞י לֹ֣א נִטְמֵ֗אתִי אַחֲרֵ֤י הַבְּעָלִים֙ לֹ֣א הָלַ֔כְתִּי רְאִ֤י דַרְכֵּךְ֙ בַּגַּ֔יְא דְּעִ֖י מֶ֣ה עָשִׂ֑ית בִּכְרָ֥ה קַלָּ֖ה מְשָׂרֶ֥כֶת דְּרָכֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: How can you say, Not I am defiled, after the Baals not I have walked? See your way in the valley; know what you have done: a young camel swift crisscrossing her ways.

en.L: How can you say, "I am not defiled, I have not gone after the Baals"? \q Look at your way in the valley; \q know what you have done, \q you swift young camel crisscrossing her ways!
en.B: How can you say, "I have not made myself unclean, I have not gone after the Baals"? \q Look at your path in the valley; \q admit what you have done, \q you restless young she-camel, running this way and that!
en.R: How can you say, "I am not unclean. I have not followed the Baals, the false gods called Baal"? \q Look at what you did in the valley, and admit it. \q You are like a young female camel \q running wildly in every direction.

es.L: ¿Cómo puedes decir: «No estoy contaminada, no he andado tras los baales»? \q Mira tu camino en el valle; \q reconoce lo que has hecho, \q ¡camella joven y ligera que entrecruza sus caminos!
es.B: ¿Cómo puedes decir: «No me he hecho impura, no he ido tras los baales»? \q Mira tu rastro en el valle; \q reconoce lo que has hecho, \q ¡camella joven e inquieta que corre de un lado a otro!
es.R: ¿Cómo puedes decir: «No soy impura. No he seguido a los baales, los dioses falsos llamados Baal»? \q Mira lo que hiciste en el valle, y admítelo. \q Eres como una camella joven \q que corre como loca en todas direcciones.

fr.L: Comment peux-tu dire : « Je ne me suis pas souillée, \q je ne suis pas allée derrière les Baals » ? \q Regarde ta conduite dans la vallée ; \q reconnais ce que tu as fait, \q chamelle rapide qui entrecroise ses chemins !
fr.B: Comment peux-tu dire : « Je ne me suis pas rendue impure, \q je n’ai pas suivi les Baals » ? \q Regarde ton chemin dans la vallée ; \q avoue ce que tu as fait, \q jeune chamelle agitée qui court en tous sens !
fr.R: Comment peux-tu dire : « Je ne suis pas impure. \q Je n’ai pas suivi les Baals, les faux dieux appelés Baal » ? \q Regarde ce que tu as fait dans la vallée, et avoue-le. \q Tu es comme une jeune chamelle \q qui court follement dans toutes les directions.

sw.L: Unawezaje kusema, "Sijatiwa unajisi, sijawafuata Mabaali"? \q Tazama njia yako bondeni; \q jua ulichokifanya, \q wewe ngamia jike mwepesi akikatiza njia zake!
sw.B: Unawezaje kusema, "Sijajitia unajisi, sijawafuata Mabaali"? \q Itazame njia yako bondeni; \q kubali ulichokifanya, \q wewe ngamia jike asiyetulia, ukikimbia huku na huko!
sw.R: Unawezaje kusema, "Mimi si najisi. Sijawafuata Mabaali, miungu ya uongo iitwayo Baali"? \q Tazama uliyoyafanya bondeni, nawe ukiri. \q Wewe ni kama ngamia jike mchanga \q anayekimbia ovyo kila upande.

vi.L: Sao ngươi có thể nói: "Tôi không bị ô uế, tôi đã không đi theo các Ba-anh"? \q Hãy nhìn đường lối ngươi trong thung lũng; \q hãy biết điều ngươi đã làm, \q hỡi lạc đà cái tơ chạy nhanh, chạy ngang chạy dọc trên đường mình!
vi.B: Sao ngươi có thể nói: "Tôi đâu có làm mình ô uế, tôi đâu có đi theo các Ba-anh"? \q Hãy nhìn con đường của ngươi trong thung lũng; \q hãy nhận điều ngươi đã làm, \q hỡi lạc đà cái tơ hiếu động, chạy tới chạy lui!
vi.R: Sao ngươi có thể nói: "Tôi không ô uế. Tôi không đi theo các Ba-anh, là những thần giả mang tên Ba-anh"? \q Hãy nhìn xem ngươi đã làm gì trong thung lũng và hãy nhận tội đi. \q Ngươi giống như một con lạc đà cái non \q chạy cuồng loạn khắp mọi hướng.

ko.L: 네가 어떻게 "나는 더럽혀지지 않았다. 나는 바알들을 따라가지 않았다" 하고 말할 수 있느냐? \q 골짜기에 있는 네 길을 보아라. \q 네가 무엇을 했는지 알아라. \q 너는 제 길을 이리저리 엇갈려 달리는 날랜 어린 암낙타다!
ko.B: 네가 어떻게 "나는 나를 더럽히지 않았다. 바알들을 따라가지 않았다" 하고 말할 수 있느냐? \q 골짜기에 난 네 발자취를 보아라. \q 네가 한 일을 인정하여라. \q 너는 이리저리 날뛰는 들뜬 어린 암낙타다!
ko.R: 네가 어떻게 "나는 더럽지 않다. 나는 바알들, 곧 바알이라는 거짓 신들을 따라가지 않았다" 하고 말할 수 있느냐? \q 골짜기에서 네가 한 짓을 보고 그것을 인정하여라. \q 너는 어린 암낙타와 같다. \q 사방으로 정신없이 뛰어다니는 낙타다.

decisions.choice: the Baals: the many local forms of Baal
decisions.reason: Baal was the Canaanite god of storm and harvest. The plural names the many shrines and images under which he was worshiped, each town with its own (verse 28; Judges 2:11).

decisions.choice: the valley: probably the Valley of Ben-hinnom
decisions.reason: The valley is not named. It is most likely the Valley of Ben-hinnom outside Jerusalem, where children were burned as sacrifices at Topheth (7:31; 19:2-6; 2 Kings 23:10). Judah's denial of verse 23 cannot stand against what was done there.

decisions.choice: a swift young camel crisscrossing her ways: restless, aimless running
decisions.reason: A young she-camel, not yet trained, runs back and forth with no sense of direction. The picture is of Israel running from one god to another; the next verse turns to an animal driven by desire.

decisions.choice: the Baals, the false gods called Baal
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *ba'alim* at Readable explains who the Baals are (m1).

decisions.choice: admit what you have done / running this way and that / running wildly in every direction
decisions.reason: "Know" here means to recognize and own up to, and Balanced and Readable say so. They give the sense of the rare verb for the camel's crossing tracks (m3).

decisions.choice: "los baales" (L, B); "los baales, los dioses falsos llamados Baal" (R)
decisions.reason: The Baals as the terms note sets them for Spanish; Readable explains them as the English does.

decisions.choice: Mabaali
decisions.reason: The plural "the Baals" is "Mabaali", as 1 Samuel 7:4 and 1 Kings 18:18; Readable explains it as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "les Baals" (L, B); "les Baals, les faux dieux appelés Baal" (R), for the whole book
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *baʿalim*; Readable explains who they are, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "các Ba-anh"
decisions.reason: The published form (1 Kings 18:18; 2 Chronicles 17:3); Readable adds that they are false gods, as the English Readable does.

source.text: פֶּ֣רֶה׀לִמֻּ֣ד מִדְבָּ֗ר בְּאַוַּ֤ת נַפְשָׁהּ֙ שָׁאֲפָ֣ה ר֔וּחַ תַּאֲנָתָ֖הּ מִ֣י יְשִׁיבֶ֑נָּה כָּל־מְבַקְשֶׁ֨יהָ֙ לֹ֣א יִיעָ֔פוּ בְּחָדְשָׁ֖הּ יִמְצָאֽוּנְהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: A wild donkey used to [the] wilderness, in [the] desire of her soul she sniffs [the] wind; her heat, who can turn her back? All seeking her will not tire themselves; in her month they will find her.

en.L: A wild donkey used to the wilderness, in her desire she sniffs the wind; \q in her heat, who can turn her back? \q All who seek her will not weary themselves; \q in her month they will find her.
en.B: A wild donkey at home in the wilderness sniffs the wind in her longing. \q In her season of heat, who can turn her back? \q The males that seek her need not tire themselves; \q at mating time they will find her.
en.R: You are like a wild female donkey that lives in the desert. When she wants a mate, she sniffs the wind. \q When she is in heat, no one can hold her back. \q The males that look for her do not need to wear themselves out. \q When her season comes, they will find her easily.

es.L: Asna montés acostumbrada al desierto, en el deseo de su alma olfatea el viento; \q en su celo, ¿quién la hará volver? \q Todos los que la buscan no se cansarán; \q en su mes la hallarán.
es.B: Una asna montés, hecha al desierto, olfatea el viento en su anhelo. \q En su tiempo de celo, ¿quién la puede hacer volver? \q Los machos que la buscan no necesitan cansarse; \q en el tiempo del apareamiento la encontrarán.
es.R: Eres como una burra salvaje que vive en el desierto. Cuando quiere aparearse, olfatea el viento. \q Cuando está en celo, nadie la puede detener. \q Los machos que la buscan no necesitan agotarse. \q Cuando llega su tiempo, la encuentran fácilmente.

fr.L: Ânesse sauvage habituée au désert, dans le désir de son âme elle aspire le vent ; \q son rut, qui la fera revenir ? \q Tous ceux qui la cherchent ne se fatigueront pas ; \q en son mois ils la trouveront.
fr.B: Ânesse sauvage à l’aise dans le désert, elle hume le vent dans son ardeur. \q Quand elle est en chaleur, qui peut la retenir ? \q Les mâles qui la cherchent n’ont pas à se fatiguer ; \q au temps de l’accouplement, ils la trouveront.
fr.R: Tu es comme une ânesse sauvage qui vit dans le désert. Quand elle veut un mâle, elle renifle le vent. \q Quand elle est en chaleur, personne ne peut la retenir. \q Les mâles qui la cherchent n’ont pas besoin de se fatiguer. \q Quand sa saison arrive, ils la trouvent facilement.

sw.L: Punda-mwitu aliyezoea nyika, kwa tamaa ya nafsi yake huinusa pepo; \q katika joto lake, ni nani awezaye kumrudisha? \q Wote wamtafutao hawatajichosha; \q katika mwezi wake watampata.
sw.B: Punda-mwitu jike aliyezoea nyika huinusa pepo kwa tamaa yake. \q Wakati wa joto lake, ni nani awezaye kumzuia? \q Madume wanaomtafuta hawahitaji kujichosha; \q wakati wa kupandana watampata.
sw.R: Wewe ni kama punda-mwitu jike anayeishi jangwani. Anapotaka dume, huinusa pepo. \q Anapokuwa katika joto lake, hakuna anayeweza kumzuia. \q Madume wanaomtafuta hawahitaji kujichosha. \q Wakati wake ukifika, watampata kwa urahisi.

vi.L: Một con lừa rừng quen nơi hoang mạc, theo dục vọng của nó, nó hít gió; \q trong lúc động đực, ai có thể ngăn nó lại? \q Mọi con tìm nó sẽ không phải mệt nhọc; \q vào tháng của nó, chúng sẽ tìm được nó.
vi.B: Con lừa rừng quen sống nơi hoang mạc hít hơi gió trong cơn thèm khát. \q Khi nó động đực, ai cản nó lại được? \q Những con đực tìm nó chẳng cần nhọc công; \q đến mùa giao phối, chúng sẽ gặp nó.
vi.R: Ngươi giống như một con lừa cái hoang sống trong sa mạc. Khi muốn có bạn tình, nó hít hơi gió. \q Khi nó động đực, không ai giữ nó lại được. \q Những con đực đi tìm nó chẳng cần mệt sức. \q Khi đến mùa, chúng sẽ dễ dàng tìm thấy nó.

ko.L: 광야에 익숙한 들나귀가 제 욕정에 바람을 들이마신다. \q 그 암컷의 발정을 누가 돌이킬 수 있겠느냐? \q 그것을 찾는 자들은 모두 수고할 필요가 없다. \q 그 달에 그들이 그것을 찾아낼 것이다.
ko.B: 광야에서 사는 들나귀가 욕정에 차서 바람 냄새를 맡는다. \q 발정기에 누가 그것을 막을 수 있겠느냐? \q 그것을 찾는 수컷들은 애쓸 필요가 없다. \q 짝짓기 때가 되면 그것을 찾아낼 것이다.
ko.R: 너는 광야에 사는 암컷 들나귀와 같다. 짝을 찾을 때에는 바람 냄새를 맡는다. \q 발정이 나면 아무도 그것을 붙잡아 둘 수 없다. \q 그것을 찾는 수컷들은 힘들여 애쓸 필요가 없다. \q 때가 되면 쉽게 그것을 찾아낸다.

decisions.choice: a wild donkey in heat: a female driven by her own desire
decisions.reason: A female wild donkey in her season goes looking for males and sniffs the wind for their scent. No one can stop her, and the males do not have to search for her. The picture is plain: Israel is not lured away by other gods; she goes after them herself.

decisions.choice: a wild donkey ... her: the female
decisions.reason: The noun is the ordinary word for a wild donkey, but every pronoun and verb that follows is feminine, so a female is meant. The written text has "his desire" and the reading tradition "her desire"; the reading tradition agrees with the rest of the verse.

decisions.choice: her month: her mating season
decisions.reason: "Her month" is the time of year when she is in season.

decisions.choice: the males that seek her / You are like ... / at mating time
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who seeks her and what "her month" means (m3). Readable adds "You are like" to tie the picture to Israel, as verse 23 does.

source.text: מִנְעִ֤י רַגְלֵךְ֙ מִיָּחֵ֔ף וּגְרוֹנֵ֖ךְ מִצִּמְאָ֑ה וַתֹּאמְרִ֣י נוֹאָ֔שׁ ל֕וֹא כִּֽי־אָהַ֥בְתִּי זָרִ֖ים וְאַחֲרֵיהֶ֥ם אֵלֵֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Keep your foot from bare and your throat from thirst; but you said, Hopeless! No! For I love strangers, and after them I will go.

en.L: Keep your foot from going bare \q and your throat from thirst. \q But you said, "It is hopeless! \q No, for I have loved strangers, \q and after them I will go."
en.B: Do not run until your feet are bare \q and your throat is dry with thirst. \q But you said, "It is no use! \q No, I love strangers, \q and I will go after them."
en.R: Stop running after them until your sandals wear out \q and your throat is dry with thirst! \q But you said, "It is no use! \q No! I love those foreign gods, \q and I will keep following them."

es.L: Guarda tu pie de andar descalzo \q y tu garganta de la sed. \q Pero dijiste: «¡No hay remedio! \q No, porque he amado a extraños, \q y tras ellos iré».
es.B: No corras hasta quedarte descalza \q y con la garganta seca de sed. \q Pero dijiste: «¡Es inútil! \q No, yo amo a los extraños, \q y tras ellos iré».
es.R: ¡Deja de correr tras ellos hasta que se te gasten las sandalias \q y se te seque la garganta de sed! \q Pero dijiste: «¡Es inútil! \q ¡No! Amo a esos dioses extranjeros, \q y los seguiré».

fr.L: Garde ton pied de la nudité \q et ta gorge de la soif. \q Mais tu as dit : « C’est désespéré ! \q Non, car j’aime les étrangers, \q et derrière eux j’irai. »
fr.B: Ne cours pas jusqu’à avoir les pieds nus \q et la gorge desséchée par la soif. \q Mais tu as dit : « Inutile ! \q Non, j’aime les étrangers, \q et je les suivrai. »
fr.R: Arrête de leur courir après jusqu’à user tes sandales \q et à avoir la gorge sèche de soif ! \q Mais tu as dit : « Ça ne sert à rien ! \q Non ! J’aime ces dieux étrangers, \q et je continuerai à les suivre. »

sw.L: Zuia mguu wako usiwe bila kiatu, \q na koo lako lisiwe na kiu. \q Lakini ulisema, "Hakuna tumaini! \q Hapana, kwa maana nimewapenda wageni, \q nami nitawafuata."
sw.B: Usikimbie mpaka miguu yako ikose viatu \q na koo lako likauke kwa kiu. \q Lakini ulisema, "Haifai kitu! \q Hapana, ninawapenda wageni, \q nami nitawafuata."
sw.R: Acha kuwakimbilia mpaka viatu vyako vichakae \q na koo lako likauke kwa kiu! \q Lakini ulisema, "Haifai kitu! \q Hapana! Ninaipenda miungu hiyo ya kigeni, \q nami nitaendelea kuifuata."

vi.L: Hãy giữ chân ngươi khỏi trần trụi \q và cổ họng ngươi khỏi khát. \q Nhưng ngươi đã nói: "Vô ích thôi! \q Không, vì tôi đã yêu những kẻ lạ, \q và tôi sẽ đi theo chúng."
vi.B: Đừng chạy cho đến khi chân ngươi trần trụi \q và cổ họng ngươi khô vì khát. \q Nhưng ngươi đã nói: "Vô ích thôi! \q Không, tôi yêu những kẻ lạ, \q và tôi sẽ đi theo chúng."
vi.R: Hãy thôi chạy theo chúng cho đến khi mòn cả dép \q và cổ họng khô khát! \q Nhưng ngươi đã nói: "Vô ích thôi! \q Không! Tôi yêu những thần ngoại bang ấy, \q và tôi sẽ cứ đi theo chúng."

ko.L: 네 발을 맨발이 되지 않게 하고, \q 네 목을 목마르지 않게 하여라. \q 그러나 너는 말했다. "소용없다! \q 아니다, 나는 낯선 자들을 사랑했으니 \q 그들을 따라가겠다."
ko.B: 발이 맨발이 되도록 \q 목이 타도록 달려가지 마라. \q 그러나 너는 말했다. "소용없다! \q 아니다, 나는 낯선 신들을 사랑한다. \q 나는 그들을 따라가겠다."
ko.R: 신발이 다 닳도록, \q 목이 바싹 마르도록 그들을 쫓아다니지 마라! \q 그러나 너는 말했다. "소용없다! \q 아니다! 나는 그 다른 나라 신들을 사랑한다. \q 나는 계속 그들을 따라가겠다."

decisions.choice: keep your foot from going bare: stop wearing yourself out in the chase
decisions.reason: Running after lovers until her sandals wear through and her throat is parched pictures the endless effort Israel spends on other gods and foreign help. God tells her to stop.

decisions.choice: strangers: foreign gods
decisions.reason: "Strangers" are the foreign gods Israel loves as lovers (3:13; Deuteronomy 32:16). The word may also take in the foreign nations she courts (verse 18).

decisions.choice: hopeless: there is no use trying
decisions.reason: The word means despairing, giving up. Israel answers God's call by saying she cannot stop and will not (18:12).

decisions.choice: stop running after them until your sandals wear out ... those foreign gods
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the bare foot (m1) and says who the strangers are (m2).

source.text: כְּבֹ֤שֶׁת גַּנָּב֙ כִּ֣י יִמָּצֵ֔א כֵּ֥ן הֹבִ֖ישׁוּ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל הֵ֤מָּה מַלְכֵיהֶם֙ שָֽׂרֵיהֶ֔ם וְכֹהֲנֵיהֶ֖ם וּנְבִיאֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: As [the] shame of a thief when he is found, so are put to shame [the] house of Israel, they, their kings, their princes, and their priests, and their prophets,

en.L: As a thief is ashamed when he is caught, \q so the house of Israel is put to shame: \q they, their kings, their princes, \q and their priests and their prophets,
en.B: As a thief is shamed when he is found out, \q so the house of Israel is put to shame: \q they, their kings and their officials, \q their priests and their prophets,
en.R: A thief feels ashamed when he is caught. \q In the same way, the people of Israel are ashamed, \q together with their kings and leaders, \q their priests and their prophets.

es.L: Como se avergüenza el ladrón cuando es sorprendido, \q así es avergonzada la casa de Israel: \q ellos, sus reyes, sus príncipes, \q y sus sacerdotes y sus profetas,
es.B: Como queda en vergüenza el ladrón cuando lo descubren, \q así queda en vergüenza la casa de Israel: \q ellos, sus reyes y sus jefes, \q sus sacerdotes y sus profetas,
es.R: Un ladrón siente vergüenza cuando lo atrapan. \q De la misma manera, el pueblo de Israel está avergonzado, \q junto con sus reyes y sus dirigentes, \q sus sacerdotes y sus profetas.

fr.L: Comme la honte du voleur quand il est pris, \q ainsi est couverte de honte la maison d’Israël, \q eux, leurs rois, leurs princes, \q et leurs prêtres et leurs prophètes,
fr.B: Comme un voleur est couvert de honte quand on le surprend, \q ainsi la maison d’Israël est couverte de honte, \q eux, leurs rois et leurs chefs, \q leurs prêtres et leurs prophètes,
fr.R: Un voleur a honte quand on l’attrape. \q De la même façon, le peuple d’Israël a honte, \q avec ses rois et ses chefs, \q ses prêtres et ses prophètes.

sw.L: Kama aibu ya mwizi akamatwapo, \q ndivyo nyumba ya Israeli inavyoaibishwa: \q wao, wafalme wao, wakuu wao, \q na makuhani wao, na manabii wao,
sw.B: Kama mwizi anavyoaibika anapogunduliwa, \q ndivyo nyumba ya Israeli inavyoaibishwa: \q wao, wafalme wao na maafisa wao, \q makuhani wao na manabii wao,
sw.R: Mwizi huona aibu anapokamatwa. \q Vivyo hivyo watu wa Israeli wameaibika, \q pamoja na wafalme wao na viongozi wao, \q makuhani wao na manabii wao.

vi.L: Như kẻ trộm xấu hổ khi bị bắt, \q nhà Y-sơ-ra-ên cũng bị hổ thẹn như vậy: \q chúng, các vua chúng, các quan trưởng chúng, \q các thầy tế lễ và các nhà tiên tri của chúng,
vi.B: Như kẻ trộm bị nhục khi bị bắt quả tang, \q nhà Y-sơ-ra-ên cũng bị hổ thẹn như vậy: \q chúng, các vua và các quan chức, \q các thầy tế lễ và các nhà tiên tri của chúng,
vi.R: Kẻ trộm thấy xấu hổ khi bị bắt. \q Cũng vậy, dân Y-sơ-ra-ên phải hổ thẹn, \q cùng với các vua và các nhà lãnh đạo, \q các thầy tế lễ và các nhà tiên tri của họ.

ko.L: 도둑이 붙잡힐 때 수치를 당하듯이, \q 이스라엘 집이 수치를 당했다. \q 그들과 그들의 왕들과 그들의 고관들과 \q 그들의 제사장들과 그들의 예언자들이,
ko.B: 도둑이 들킬 때 망신을 당하듯이 \q 이스라엘 집이 수치를 당했다. \q 그들과 그들의 왕들과 관리들, \q 그들의 제사장들과 예언자들이 그러하다.
ko.R: 도둑은 붙잡히면 부끄러워한다. \q 그와 마찬가지로 이스라엘 백성도 부끄러움을 당한다. \q 그들의 왕들과 지도자들, \q 그들의 제사장들과 예언자들도 함께 부끄러움을 당한다.

decisions.choice: the shame of a thief when he is caught: exposure in public
decisions.reason: A thief caught in the act has no excuse and is shamed before everyone (Exodus 22:1-3). Israel had denied its idolatry (verse 23), but it has been caught.

decisions.choice: is put to shame: the verb treats the shame as certain
decisions.reason: The verb has the form for something done, as though the disgrace has already fallen. It may describe the shame Judah already feels or the shame that is surely coming.

decisions.choice: their kings, their princes, their priests, their prophets: the whole leadership
decisions.reason: Jeremiah often names these four groups together as the ones responsible for the nation (1:18; 8:1; 32:32). None of them is spared the shame.

decisions.choice: princes (Literal); officials (Balanced); leaders (Readable)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *sar*. The sentence runs on into verse 27, so Literal and Balanced end with a comma; Readable ends the sentence here.

source.text: אֹמְרִ֨ים לָעֵ֜ץ אָ֣בִי אַ֗תָּה וְלָאֶ֨בֶן֙ אַ֣תְּ יְלִדְתָּ֔נוּ כִּֽי־פָנ֥וּ אֵלַ֛י עֹ֖רֶף וְלֹ֣א פָנִ֑ים וּבְעֵ֤ת רָֽעָתָם֙ יֹֽאמְר֔וּ ק֖וּמָה וְהוֹשִׁיעֵֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: [who] say to the tree, My father [are] you, and to the stone, You gave birth to us; for they have turned to me [the] back and not [the] face; but in [the] time of their trouble they say, Arise and save us!

en.L: who say to a tree, "You [are] my father," and to a stone, "You gave birth to us." \q For they have turned to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} the back and not the face; \q but in the time of their trouble they say, \q "Arise and save us!"
en.B: who call a tree "My father" and tell a stone, "You gave birth to us." \q They have turned their backs to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, not their faces; \q yet when trouble comes they say, \q "Rise up and save us!"
en.R: They say to a wooden idol, "You are my father." They say to a stone idol, "You are the mother who gave birth to us." \q They have turned their backs on {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and will not face {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q But when they are in trouble, they cry out to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q "Come and save us!"

es.L: que dicen a un árbol: «Mi padre [eres] tú», y a una piedra: «Tú nos diste a luz». \q Porque {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} han vuelto la espalda y no el rostro; \q pero en el tiempo de su angustia dicen: \q «¡Levántate y sálvanos!».
es.B: que a un árbol le dicen «Padre mío» y a una piedra: «Tú nos diste a luz». \q Ellos {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} han dado la espalda, no la cara; \q pero cuando llega la desgracia dicen: \q «¡Levántate y sálvanos!».
es.R: Le dicen a un ídolo de madera: «Tú eres mi padre». Le dicen a un ídolo de piedra: «Tú eres la madre que nos dio a luz». \q Ellos {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} han dado la espalda y no quieren volverse hacia {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. \q Pero cuando están en problemas, {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} gritan: \q «¡Ven a salvarnos!».

fr.L: qui disent au bois : « Tu [es] mon père », et à la pierre : « Tu nous as enfantés. » \q Car ils {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}ont tourné le dos et non la face ; \q mais au temps de leur malheur, ils disent : \q « Lève-toi et sauve-nous ! »
fr.B: eux qui appellent un arbre « Mon père » et disent à une pierre : « Tu nous as mis au monde. » \q Ils {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}ont tourné le dos, et non le visage ; \q mais quand vient le malheur, ils disent : \q « Lève-toi et sauve-nous ! »
fr.R: Ils disent à une idole en bois : « Tu es mon père. » Ils disent à une idole en pierre : « Tu es la mère qui nous a mis au monde. » \q Ils {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}ont tourné le dos et ne veulent pas {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} regarder en face. \q Mais quand ils sont dans le malheur, ils {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} crient : \q « Viens nous sauver ! »

sw.L: wanaouambia mti, "Wewe [ni] baba yangu," na jiwe, "Wewe ulituzaa." \q Kwa maana wamenigeuzia {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} kisogo, wala si uso; \q lakini wakati wa taabu yao husema, \q "Inuka utuokoe!"
sw.B: wanaouita mti "Baba yangu" na kuliambia jiwe, "Wewe ulituzaa." \q Wamenipa kisogo, wala si nyuso zao; \q lakini taabu inapowajia husema, \q "Inuka utuokoe!"
sw.R: Wanaiambia sanamu ya mti, "Wewe ni baba yangu." Wanaiambia sanamu ya jiwe, "Wewe ndiwe mama aliyetuzaa." \q Wamenipa kisogo, wala hawataki kunitazama. \q Lakini wanapokuwa katika taabu, wananililia, \q "Njoo utuokoe!"

vi.L: là những kẻ nói với khúc gỗ: "Ngươi [là] cha ta," và với hòn đá: "Ngươi đã sinh ra chúng ta." \q Vì chúng đã xoay lưng lại với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, chứ không phải mặt; \q nhưng trong lúc hoạn nạn, chúng lại nói: \q "Xin đứng dậy và cứu chúng tôi!"
vi.B: là những kẻ gọi khúc gỗ: "Cha tôi," và bảo hòn đá: "Ngươi đã sinh ra chúng tôi." \q Chúng đã quay lưng lại với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} chứ không quay mặt về {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; \q thế mà khi hoạn nạn đến, chúng lại nói: \q "Xin trỗi dậy và cứu chúng con!"
vi.R: Chúng nói với tượng gỗ: "Ngài là cha tôi." Chúng nói với tượng đá: "Ngài là mẹ đã sinh ra chúng tôi." \q Chúng đã quay lưng với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và không chịu nhìn mặt {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \q Nhưng khi gặp hoạn nạn, chúng kêu cầu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}: \q "Xin hãy đến cứu chúng con!"

ko.L: 그들은 나무에게 "너는 내 아버지다" 하고, 돌에게 "네가 우리를 낳았다" 하고 말한다. \q 그들이 나에게 등을 돌리고 얼굴을 돌리지 않았기 때문이다. \q 그러나 그들은 재난의 때에 말한다. \q "일어나서 우리를 구원해 주십시오!"
ko.B: 그들은 나무를 보고 "내 아버지"라고 부르고, 돌에게 "네가 우리를 낳았다" 하고 말한다. \q 그들은 나에게 얼굴이 아니라 등을 돌렸다. \q 그러면서도 재난이 닥치면 말한다. \q "일어나 우리를 구원해 주십시오!"
ko.R: 그들은 나무로 만든 우상에게 "당신은 내 아버지입니다" 하고 말한다. 돌로 만든 우상에게 "당신은 우리를 낳은 어머니입니다" 하고 말한다. \q 그들은 나에게 등을 돌리고 나를 쳐다보려고도 하지 않는다. \q 그러나 어려움을 당하면 나에게 부르짖는다. \q "오셔서 우리를 구해 주십시오!"

decisions.choice: a tree ... a stone: idols of wood and stone
decisions.reason: The tree is a wooden image or sacred pole and the stone a standing stone or carved idol, both used in Canaanite worship (Deuteronomy 16:21-22; 2 Kings 17:10). Calling the wooden one "father" and the stone one "mother" may be mockery, since the wooden pole usually stood for a goddess and the stone pillar for a god.

decisions.choice: the back and not the face: turning away in contempt
decisions.reason: To show someone your back is to reject them and refuse to listen (7:24; 32:33).

decisions.choice: Arise and save us!: a cry to God to act
decisions.reason: "Arise" is how Israel called on God to come to its help (Numbers 10:35; Psalm 3:8). The people who turned their backs on God still cry to him when disaster comes. Verse 28 answers with the same verb.

decisions.choice: gave birth to us: the reading tradition
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew reads "gave birth to me" and the reading tradition "to us"; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: a wooden idol ... a stone idol ... the mother ... cry out to me
decisions.reason: Readable says what the tree and stone are (m1), puts "gave birth" as "mother" beside "father", and names the one they call on (m3).

source.text: וְאַיֵּ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֣יתָ לָּ֔ךְ יָק֕וּמוּ אִם־יוֹשִׁיע֖וּךָ בְּעֵ֣ת רָעָתֶ֑ךָ כִּ֚י מִסְפַּ֣ר עָרֶ֔יךָ הָי֥וּ אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ יְהוּדָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And where [are] your gods that you made for yourself? Let them arise, if they will save you in [the] time of your trouble; for [the] number of your cities are your gods, Judah.

en.L: But where [are] your gods that you made for yourself? \q Let them arise, if they can save you \q in the time of your trouble; \q for as many as your cities \q are your gods, Judah.
en.B: Where then are the gods you made for yourself? \q Let them get up, if they can save you \q when trouble comes to you. \q For you have as many gods \q as you have towns, Judah.
en.R: Where are the gods you made for yourself? \q Let them come and save you \q when you are in trouble! \q Judah, you have as many gods \q as you have towns.

es.L: ¿Y dónde [están] tus dioses que te hiciste? \q Que se levanten, si pueden salvarte \q en el tiempo de tu angustia; \q porque tantos como tus ciudades \q son tus dioses, Judá.
es.B: ¿Dónde están, pues, los dioses que te hiciste? \q Que se levanten, si es que pueden salvarte \q cuando te llegue la desgracia. \q Porque tienes tantos dioses \q como ciudades, Judá.
es.R: ¿Dónde están los dioses que te hiciste? \q ¡Que vengan a salvarte \q cuando estés en problemas! \q Judá, tienes tantos dioses \q como ciudades.

fr.L: Mais où [sont] tes dieux que tu t’es faits ? \q Qu’ils se lèvent, s’ils peuvent te sauver \q au temps de ton malheur ; \q car autant tu as de villes, \q autant tu as de dieux, Juda.
fr.B: Où sont donc les dieux que tu t’es fabriqués ? \q Qu’ils se lèvent, s’ils peuvent te sauver \q quand le malheur te frappe ! \q Car tu as autant de dieux \q que de villes, Juda.
fr.R: Où sont les dieux que tu t’es fabriqués ? \q Qu’ils viennent te sauver \q quand tu es dans le malheur ! \q Juda, tu as autant de dieux \q que de villes.

sw.L: Lakini iko wapi miungu yako uliyojifanyia? \q Na iinuke, kama inaweza kukuokoa \q wakati wa taabu yako; \q kwa maana kama hesabu ya miji yako \q ndivyo ilivyo miungu yako, Yuda.
sw.B: Iko wapi basi miungu uliyojitengenezea? \q Na iinuke, kama inaweza kukuokoa \q taabu inapokujia. \q Kwa maana una miungu mingi \q kama ulivyo na miji, ee Yuda.
sw.R: Iko wapi miungu uliyojitengenezea? \q Na ije ikuokoe \q unapokuwa katika taabu! \q Ee Yuda, una miungu mingi \q kama ulivyo na miji.

vi.L: Vậy các thần ngươi đã làm cho mình ở đâu? \q Hãy để chúng đứng dậy, nếu chúng có thể cứu ngươi \q trong lúc ngươi hoạn nạn; \q vì số thần của ngươi \q nhiều như số thành của ngươi, hỡi Giu-đa.
vi.B: Vậy các thần ngươi đã làm cho mình ở đâu? \q Hãy để chúng đứng dậy, nếu chúng cứu được ngươi \q khi hoạn nạn đến với ngươi. \q Vì ngươi có bao nhiêu thành \q thì có bấy nhiêu thần, hỡi Giu-đa.
vi.R: Các thần ngươi tự làm ra cho mình ở đâu rồi? \q Hãy để chúng đến cứu ngươi \q khi ngươi gặp hoạn nạn! \q Hỡi Giu-đa, ngươi có bao nhiêu thành \q thì có bấy nhiêu thần.

ko.L: 그러면 네가 너를 위해 만든 네 신들은 어디 있느냐? \q 그들이 일어나라. 그들이 너를 구원할 수 있다면, \q 네 재난의 때에. \q 네 성읍의 수만큼 \q 네 신들이 있기 때문이다, 유다야.
ko.B: 네가 스스로 만든 신들은 그렇다면 어디 있느냐? \q 그들이 너를 구원할 수 있다면 일어나 보라고 하여라. \q 네게 재난이 닥쳤을 때 말이다. \q 유다야, 너는 성읍의 수만큼이나 \q 많은 신을 두었다.
ko.R: 네가 만든 신들은 어디 있느냐? \q 네가 어려움을 당할 때 \q 그들이 와서 너를 구해 보라고 하여라! \q 유다야, 너는 성읍의 수만큼이나 \q 많은 신을 가지고 있다.

decisions.choice: let them arise: God answers the people's cry with their own word
decisions.reason: The people cry "Arise" to God (verse 27); God tells them to say it to the gods they made. The challenge mocks idols that cannot move or save (Deuteronomy 32:37-38; Isaiah 46:7).

decisions.choice: as many as your cities are your gods: every town with its own god
decisions.reason: Each town had its own shrines and its own local gods (11:13). The many gods could not do together what the one God had done.

decisions.choice: let them get up / let them come and save you; as many gods as you have towns
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the play on "arise" with "rise up" and "get up"; Readable gives the sense. The comparison of gods and towns is put in natural order.

decisions.choice: "tu" for Judah here
decisions.reason: The Hebrew addresses Judah in the masculine singular in verse 28, after the feminine of verses 16-25; French "tu" serves for both, with masculine agreement where an adjective is needed.

source.text: לָ֥מָּה תָרִ֖יבוּ אֵלָ֑י כֻּלְּכֶ֛ם פְּשַׁעְתֶּ֥ם בִּ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Why do you contend against me? All of you have rebelled against me, declares Yahweh.

en.L: Why do you contend with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? \q All of you have rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Why do you bring charges against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}? \q You have all rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Why do you take {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} to court? \q All of you have turned against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: ¿Por qué {{plural_you:litigan|litigáis}} contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}? \q Todos {{plural_you:ustedes se han rebelado|vosotros os habéis rebelado}} contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: ¿Por qué {{plural_you:presentan|presentáis}} cargos contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}? \q Todos {{plural_you:ustedes se han rebelado|vosotros os habéis rebelado}} contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: ¿Por qué {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:llevan|lleváis}} a juicio? \q Todos {{plural_you:ustedes se han puesto|vosotros os habéis puesto}} en contra de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Pourquoi plaidez-vous contre {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ? \q Vous tous, vous vous êtes révoltés contre {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Pourquoi portez-vous plainte contre {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ? \q Vous vous êtes tous révoltés contre {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} faites-vous un procès ? \q Vous vous êtes tous retournés contre {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Mbona mnashindana nami? \q Ninyi nyote mmeniasi, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Mbona mnanishtaki? \q Ninyi nyote mmeniasi, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Kwa nini mnanipeleka mahakamani? \q Ninyi nyote mmegeuka dhidi yangu, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

vi.L: Sao các ngươi tranh tụng với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}? \q Tất cả các ngươi đều đã phản nghịch {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.B: Sao các ngươi buộc tội {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}? \q Tất cả các ngươi đều đã phản nghịch {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.R: Sao các ngươi đưa {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ra tòa? \q Tất cả các ngươi đều đã chống lại {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán.

ko.L: 너희가 어찌하여 나와 다투느냐? \q 너희가 모두 나를 거역했다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다.
ko.B: 너희가 어찌하여 나를 고발하느냐? \q 너희가 모두 나를 거역했다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.R: 너희가 왜 나를 재판에 넘기려 하느냐? \q 너희는 모두 나에게 등을 돌렸다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.

decisions.choice: contend: bring a case against
decisions.reason: The verb is the courtroom word of verse 9. God brought his case against the people; now they try to bring a case against him, complaining that he has wronged them (verse 35). God answers that the guilt is theirs.

decisions.choice: rebelled: broken faith with their lord
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a subject breaking away from his overlord (verse 8; Isaiah 1:2). All of them, not only the leaders, have done it.

decisions.choice: contend / bring charges / take me to court
decisions.reason: The same wording as verse 9, so the reader sees the same lawsuit word turned around.

source.text: לַשָּׁוְא֙ הִכֵּ֣יתִי אֶת־בְּנֵיכֶ֔ם מוּסָ֖ר לֹ֣א לָקָ֑חוּ אָכְלָ֧ה חַרְבְּכֶ֛ם נְבִֽיאֵיכֶ֖ם כְּאַרְיֵ֥ה מַשְׁחִֽית׃

records.literal_gloss: In vain I struck your children; correction not they accepted; devoured your sword your prophets like a lion destroying.

en.L: In vain I struck your children; \q they accepted no correction. \q Your sword devoured your prophets like a destroying lion.
en.B: It was no use that I struck your children; \q they would not accept discipline. \q Your own sword devoured your prophets like a ravaging lion.
en.R: I punished your people, but it did no good. \q They would not learn their lesson. \q You killed your prophets with your swords, like a lion tearing its prey.

es.L: En vano herí a {{plural_you:sus hijos|vuestros hijos}}; \q no aceptaron corrección. \q {{plural_you:Su espada|Vuestra espada}} devoró a {{plural_you:sus profetas|vuestros profetas}} como león destructor.
es.B: De nada sirvió que yo golpeara a {{plural_you:sus hijos|vuestros hijos}}; \q no quisieron aceptar la disciplina. \q {{plural_you:Su propia espada|Vuestra propia espada}} devoró a {{plural_you:sus profetas|vuestros profetas}} como un león que destroza.
es.R: Castigué a {{plural_you:su gente|vuestra gente}}, pero no sirvió de nada. \q No quisieron aprender la lección. \q {{plural_you:Ustedes mataron|Vosotros matasteis}} a {{plural_you:sus profetas|vuestros profetas}} a espada, como un león que despedaza a su presa.

fr.L: En vain j’ai frappé vos fils ; \q ils n’ont pas accepté la correction. \q Votre épée a dévoré vos prophètes comme un lion destructeur.
fr.B: C’est en vain que j’ai frappé vos fils ; \q ils n’ont pas voulu accepter la leçon. \q Votre propre épée a dévoré vos prophètes comme un lion ravageur.
fr.R: J’ai puni votre peuple, mais cela n’a servi à rien. \q Ils n’ont pas voulu comprendre la leçon. \q Vous avez tué vos prophètes avec vos épées, comme un lion qui déchire sa proie.

sw.L: Bure nimewapiga watoto wenu; \q hawakupokea marudi. \q Upanga wenu umewala manabii wenu kama simba aharibuye.
sw.B: Ilikuwa bure kuwapiga watoto wenu; \q hawakukubali kuadibishwa. \q Upanga wenu wenyewe umewala manabii wenu kama simba mwenye kuangamiza.
sw.R: Niliwaadhibu watu wenu, lakini haikusaidia kitu. \q Hawakutaka kujifunza. \q Mliwaua manabii wenu kwa panga zenu, kama simba anavyorarua mawindo yake.

vi.L: Ta đã đánh con cái các ngươi cách vô ích; \q chúng không nhận sự sửa dạy. \q Gươm của các ngươi đã nuốt các nhà tiên tri của các ngươi như sư tử hủy diệt.
vi.B: Ta đã đánh phạt con cái các ngươi mà chẳng ích gì; \q chúng không chịu nhận sự sửa phạt. \q Chính gươm các ngươi đã nuốt các nhà tiên tri của các ngươi như sư tử tàn phá.
vi.R: Ta đã trừng phạt dân các ngươi, nhưng chẳng được gì. \q Chúng không chịu học bài học của mình. \q Các ngươi đã dùng gươm giết các nhà tiên tri của mình như sư tử xé mồi.

ko.L: 내가 너희 자녀들을 친 것이 헛되었다. \q 그들은 징계를 받아들이지 않았다. \q 너희 칼이 사납게 찢는 사자처럼 너희 예언자들을 삼켰다.
ko.B: 내가 너희 자녀들을 쳤지만 소용이 없었다. \q 그들은 훈계를 받아들이지 않았다. \q 너희의 칼이 사나운 사자처럼 너희 예언자들을 삼켰다.
ko.R: 내가 너희 백성을 벌했지만 아무 소용이 없었다. \q 그들은 깨닫지 못했다. \q 너희는 먹이를 찢는 사자처럼 칼로 너희 예언자들을 죽였다.

decisions.choice: correction: discipline that teaches
decisions.reason: The word means instruction given through correction, as a father disciplines a son (Proverbs 3:11-12). God's blows were meant to bring his people back, but they would not learn (5:3; 7:28).

decisions.choice: your sword devoured your prophets: Judah killed the prophets God sent
decisions.reason: Manasseh filled Jerusalem with innocent blood (2 Kings 21:16), and Jehoiakim later killed the prophet Uriah (26:20-23). Israel's killing of its prophets is remembered in Nehemiah 9:26.

decisions.choice: your children: the people as a whole
decisions.reason: "Your children" means the people of Judah, the nation's sons and daughters, struck in war and disaster.

decisions.choice: your people ... You killed your prophets with your swords, like a lion tearing its prey
decisions.reason: Readable says "people" for "children" (m3) and puts the sword devouring as killing.

source.text: הַדּ֗וֹר אַתֶּם֙ רְא֣וּ דְבַר־יְהוָ֔ה הֲמִדְבָּ֤ר הָיִ֨יתִי֙ לְיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אִ֛ם אֶ֥רֶץ מַאְפֵּ֖לְיָ֑ה מַדּ֜וּעַ אָמְר֤וּ עַמִּי֙ רַ֔דְנוּ לֽוֹא־נָב֥וֹא ע֖וֹד אֵלֶֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: The generation, you, see [the] word of Yahweh: A wilderness have I been to Israel, or a land of deep darkness? Why have said my people, We roam free; not we will come again to you?

en.L: You, the generation, see the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: \q Have I been a wilderness to Israel, \q or a land of deep darkness? \q Why have {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people said, "We roam free; \q we will not come to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} again"?
en.B: And you, this generation, pay heed to the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: \q Have I been a desert to Israel, \q or a land of deep gloom? \q Why then do {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people say, "We wander where we please; \q we will not come back to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}"?
en.R: People of today, pay attention to the message of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: \q Have I been like a desert to Israel? \q Have I been a dark and dangerous land? \q So why do {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people say, "We are free to go where we like. \q We will never come back to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}"?

es.L: {{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}}, generación, {{plural_you:miren|mirad}} la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}: \q ¿He sido yo un desierto para Israel, \q o una tierra de densa oscuridad? \q ¿Por qué ha dicho {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo: «Andamos libres; \q no vendremos más a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}»?
es.B: Y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, gente de esta generación, {{plural_you:presten|prestad}} atención a la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}: \q ¿He sido yo un desierto para Israel, \q o una tierra de densas tinieblas? \q ¿Por qué, entonces, dice {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo: «Vagamos a nuestro antojo; \q no volveremos más a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}»?
es.R: Gente de hoy, {{plural_you:presten|prestad}} atención al mensaje {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}: \q ¿He sido yo como un desierto para Israel? \q ¿He sido una tierra oscura y peligrosa? \q Entonces, ¿por qué dice {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo: «Somos libres para ir adonde queramos. \q Nunca volveremos a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}»?

fr.L: Vous, la génération, voyez la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} : \q Ai-je été un désert pour Israël, \q ou un pays de ténèbres épaisses ? \q Pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple a-t-il dit : « Nous errons librement ; \q nous ne reviendrons plus vers {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} » ?
fr.B: Et vous, génération présente, prêtez attention à la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} : \q Ai-je été un désert pour Israël, \q ou un pays de sombres ténèbres ? \q Pourquoi donc {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple dit-il : « Nous allons où bon nous semble ; \q nous ne reviendrons plus vers {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} » ?
fr.R: Gens d’aujourd’hui, faites attention au message {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} : \q Ai-je été comme un désert pour Israël ? \q Ai-je été un pays sombre et dangereux ? \q Alors pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple dit-il : « Nous sommes libres d’aller où nous voulons. \q Nous ne reviendrons jamais vers {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} » ?

sw.L: Ninyi, kizazi, lioneni neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}: \q Je, nimekuwa jangwa kwa Israeli, \q au nchi ya giza kuu? \q Mbona watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} wamesema, "Tunatanga-tanga huru; \q hatutakuja {{deity_pronoun:kwako|Kwako}} tena"?
sw.B: Nanyi kizazi hiki, lisikilizeni neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}: \q Je, nimekuwa jangwa kwa Israeli, \q au nchi ya giza nene? \q Basi mbona watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} wanasema, "Tunazurura tupendavyo; \q hatutarudi {{deity_pronoun:kwako|Kwako}} tena"?
